content:
One of my favorite iPhone cases is back with a new look. I've used previous generations of BitmoLab's GAMEBABY case, and I fell in love with it instantly. It feels like an accessory designed specifically to evoke my sense of nostalgia. The biggest selling point of this case is that it's not an accessory you need to carry separately and remember to charge. Instead, it's a cleverly designed regular iPhone case that also doubles as a controller with physical buttons, letting you play your favorite Game Boy ROMs and more. This truly embodies the spirit of "work smart, not hard." It requires no batteries, no Bluetooth, and the setup is very simple. If you're into any form of retro game emulation, you have to try this thing.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video to see the case in action!

This case has a simple yet ingenious design. It uses a two-piece construction, with the bottom half being the controller. When you're not gaming, it feels just like a regular case. You get:

  • Physical side buttons for the lock key, volume keys, and action keys
  • Cutouts for the USB-C port, speakers, buttons, and camera controls
  • Protective edges around the screen and camera plateau
  • Hard-shell plastic protection

But the magic is in the bottom half. That's where the gaming control buttons live—they're well-made, have a solid tactile feel, and are very satisfying to press. But how exactly do they work?

How It Works

Again, the cleverness of this design is that there are zero electronics inside. So there's no pairing required. How it works is that each physical game button has a small capacitive contact point that mimics the effect of your finger touching the screen. Basically, it tricks the iPhone into thinking you're tapping the on-screen controls, but it feels like you're pressing real buttons. This is the same technology used in those cheap styluses with soft capacitive tips.

There's a simple setup process to align the physical buttons with the on-screen controls. BitmoLabs has included the necessary instructions via a QR code in the packaging. However, it requires the Delta Emulator app from the App Store to function. This app is completely free, with no in-app purchases. After downloading the app, GAMEBABY provides a downloadable custom overlay that places the emulator's virtual controls right under the physical buttons. This overlay is also free (you can use it even if you don't buy the case).

Once you've installed the overlay for the Delta emulator app, you're ready to game. You simply detach the bottom half of the case, flip it, and snap it back onto your iPhone. This aligns the control buttons over the iPhone's screen, giving you real physical buttons when playing retro games. When you're done gaming, just slide the controller part out, flip it, and snap it back in—it's a regular case again.

My Experience Using It

As I mentioned at the beginning, I have zero resistance to anything retro gaming. It hits a chord in me and makes me want to revisit those classic Pokémon games. This case not only makes gaming easier but also provides a near-frictionless experience. I don't have to remember to bring anything extra, don't need to charge it, and don't need to pair it. For me, having to remember to bring additional accessories has always been the biggest hassle with any tech accessory, so this case addresses that perfectly.

After using this case, I also feel that BitmoLabs has significantly upgraded the build quality. The buttons have excellent tactile feedback—they bounce back after being pressed, and I never hit the wrong button while gaming. I primarily used it to play through all the classic Pokémon games, so the pace is relatively slow and doesn't require super-fast reactions. Even for games that need fast reflexes, this case handles it well.

There's one trade-off to mention: there's no MagSafe functionality. Because the case is a two-piece design and the bottom half already has stuff in it, there's essentially no way to incorporate MagSafe. So if you absolutely need MagSafe on your case, this one might not be for you. That said, if you have MagSafe accessories—and I have a ton—it's easy enough to just take the case off and use your accessories. Also, there's no camera control cover, but that's not a big deal at all, though worth considering.

Price and Availability

GAMEBABY is available on the BitmoLab website and Amazon, starting at $24.99. There are three versions: GameBaby Color, GameBaby Retro, and the new GameBaby Transparent (the one I'm showing). GameBaby Transparent is only available for iPhone 17 Pro Max, and only 500 units are being produced, available exclusively through the BitmoLab website. The other versions are available for iPhone 15 Pro and later models, and can be bought on Amazon or the website. Again, because there are no electronics, batteries, or Bluetooth, they can keep the price down to $25—for a case, that's an absolute steal!

Conclusion

If you're like me and love revisiting retro games on your iPhone, this case is a no-brainer. It's affordable, lightweight, easy to set up, and genuinely enhances the experience of playing emulated retro games on your iPhone. When you combine the physical buttons with iPhone's excellent haptic engine, it feels like you're actually playing a retro game console. Right now, with the hype around the new Pokémon releases, this is the perfect time to easily enjoy those games with physical buttons on your iPhone.

What do you think of this case? Would you consider getting one? Have you used one before? Let me know in the comments below!
